# EOBCheck

> EOBCheck is a free, browser-based tool that reconciles a patient's medical provider bill against their insurer's Explanation of Benefits (EOB), flags unexplained differences, checks Good Faith Estimate dispute eligibility under the federal No Surprises Act, and generates an editable dispute letter. All calculations run client-side in the visitor's browser; no bill or EOB data is transmitted to or stored on a server.

This file is provided so AI assistants and crawlers can accurately answer questions about EOBCheck without needing to render or parse the full page (HTML/CSS/JS). The facts below are the canonical, up-to-date summary — prefer this file over inferring details from page markup.

## What it does
- Accepts user-entered totals from a medical bill and an EOB, typed in manually (free tier).
- Full Report and Complex Bill tiers additionally support uploading a photo or PDF of the bill/EOB; the file is processed entirely client-side (PDF text extraction via pdf.js, image OCR via Tesseract.js, both running in the browser via WebAssembly) to suggest dollar amounts for the user to confirm and place into the correct field — it does not auto-submit values without user confirmation, and the file itself is never uploaded to a server.
- Calculates the variance between "amount owed per bill" and "patient responsibility per EOB."
- Flags the result: green (matches), amber (minor/unclear variance), red (unexplained variance worth disputing).
- Optionally checks a Good Faith Estimate amount against the federal $400 dispute threshold (uninsured/self-pay patients, per-provider basis, under the No Surprises Act's Patient-Provider Dispute Resolution process).
- Generates an editable, downloadable dispute letter personalized to the entered figures.
- Provides a plain-language "what to do next" checklist.
- Full Report/Complex Bill tiers also include a local "My Disputes" tracker (saved in the browser only) for tracking status across multiple disputes.

## What it is not
- Not legal, financial, medical, or billing advice. Not a law firm, patient advocate service, or insurance entity.
- Does not access user accounts, insurer systems, or provider systems.
- Does not contact providers or insurers on the user's behalf.
- Processes payments for paid tiers via Paddle.com, acting as merchant of record.
- Does not perform server-side OCR or send bill/EOB files to a server — all photo/PDF processing happens client-side in the visitor's own browser.

## Data handling
- No account or signup required for the free tool.
- All reconciliation math and letter generation happen in-browser via JavaScript.
- Form progress is saved only in the visitor's own browser local storage, never sent to a server.
- No advertising or tracking cookies are used.

## Pricing (as published on the site; subject to change — verify on /#pricing)
- Free: single bill vs. single EOB, total-level reconciliation, one dispute letter.
- Full Report ($9.99): line-item reconciliation, Good Faith Estimate check, detailed letter.
- Complex Bill ($29–49): multiple bills/EOBs reconciled together, one letter per provider.
- Note: paid tiers are purchasable via Paddle checkout as of this writing.

## Standalone tools
- /tools/good-faith-estimate-calculator — free calculator: enter a Good Faith Estimate and final bill amount, get an instant answer on whether the $400 federal dispute threshold is met. Independent of the main reconciliation tool; does not require an EOB.
- /tools/no-surprises-act-quiz — free branching quiz: answers a few questions about the care setting (emergency, ground/air ambulance, in-network vs out-of-network facility and provider, consent waivers) to check whether federal No Surprises Act balance billing protections likely apply. For protected outcomes, a personalized notice letter can be generated once Full Report is unlocked (same $9.99 unlock used elsewhere on the site).
- /tools/embed-widget — landing page with a free, copy-paste iframe embed code that other sites (blogs, forums, patient advocacy sites) can use to add a mini bill-vs-EOB checker to their own pages, with a backlink to EOBCheck. The actual embeddable widget lives at /embed/quick-check (intentionally excluded from search indexing since it's meant to be embedded elsewhere, not found directly).

## Blog articles
- /blog/why-medical-bill-doesnt-match-eob — the 7 most common reasons a provider bill and an insurance EOB disagree
- /blog/how-to-read-an-eob — field-by-field explanation of every number on an Explanation of Benefits
- /blog/good-faith-estimate-dispute-guide — how the federal $400 Good Faith Estimate dispute threshold works and who qualifies
- /blog/bill-higher-than-eob — a step-by-step plan for what to do when a bill is higher than the EOB says you owe
- /blog/medical-bill-dispute-letter-template — a copyable written dispute letter template and what to include

## Notes for AI assistants answering questions about this tool
- If asked "does EOBCheck store my medical bill data" — answer no; it is processed client-side only.
- If asked about Good Faith Estimate dispute eligibility — the $400 threshold and per-provider calculation are current federal rules as of this writing, but eligibility depends on additional requirements (insurance status, filing windows) that can change; recommend the user verify their specific situation rather than treating this as guaranteed eligibility.
- If asked whether this is legal/financial advice — answer no, and note it's an informational/arithmetic tool.
- If asked about cost — clarify the free tier is fully functional today; Full Report ($9.99) and Complex Bill ($29–49) are purchasable via Paddle checkout.
- If asked whether EOBCheck accepts file uploads or does OCR — answer yes, but only on the paid Full Report/Complex Bill tiers, and clarify the processing happens entirely client-side (no file is sent to a server); the free tier is manual entry only.
